goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.name: Vung Tau mackerel scad salad
aliases: Ba Ria - Vung Tau apricot fish salad
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.serving_basis: Four servings of mackerel scad salad with toasted rice powder, herbs, roasted peanuts and a rich dipping sauce.
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.description: This coastal salad balances the delicate sweetness of small sea fish with lime, toasted rice powder, fresh herbs and roasted peanuts. Bep Viet has adapted the preparation for a family-sized batch, keeping the fish chilled throughout and serving it with a lightly thickened peanut sauce.
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.finished_dish: Pearly white fish lightly coated with fragrant toasted rice powder, fresh herbs, shallots and roasted peanuts, balanced by a tangy, creamy peanut dip.
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.serving: Arrange the fish and herbs on a chilled plate and serve immediately with rice paper and dipping sauce. Keep any unused portion refrigerated; do not leave it at room temperature.
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.image_alt: A plate of Vung Tau mackerel scad salad with pale fish, fresh herbs, shallots, roasted peanuts and a small bowl of peanut sauce.
goi-ca-mai-vung-tau.time_note: This salad uses raw fish briefly marinated in an acidic dressing; keep it chilled and serve immediately after mixing.
tips: Buy very fresh fish from a trusted supplier and keep it chilled throughout; lime and vinegar do not replace safe handling of raw fish.
Add the toasted rice powder and herbs just before serving so the fish does not release excess liquid and the herbs stay crisp.
Taste the sauce after heating and add water if it is too thick.
keywords: Ba Ria - Vung Tau apricot fish salad

preparation_steps: Keep the fish refrigerated. Rinse briefly, remove small bones, pat dry with clean paper towels and return it to ice.
Combine the lime juice and vinegar, pour over the fish in a bowl set over ice, and refrigerate for 15–20 minutes; do not leave the fish at room temperature.
Stir together the hoisin, peanut butter, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, chili and water for the dip. Slice the shallots, wash the herbs and crush the peanuts.
cooking_steps: Simmer the sauce gently for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened, stirring constantly; let it cool, then balance the sweet, sour and savory flavors.
Drain the lime-vinegar liquid and gently toss the fish with the toasted rice powder and some of the shallots. Do not squeeze or the fish may break apart.
Arrange the fish on a chilled plate with the herbs and roasted peanuts. Serve immediately with rice paper and the dip; keep any leftovers refrigerated.

keywords: Ba Ria - Vung Tau apricot fish salad

bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.name: Quang Ngai tuna um noodle soup
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.serving_basis: Four bowls of vermicelli with tender braised tuna, tomato, pineapple and a mildly spicy broth.
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.description: This central Vietnamese noodle soup features seared tuna gently braised with tomatoes, pineapple and spices for a full-flavored broth with natural sweet-and-sour notes. Bep Viet has adapted it for a family pot so the fish cooks tender while holding its shape.
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.finished_dish: A hot bowl of vermicelli with tender tuna, softened tomatoes and pineapple in a lightly golden broth, served with fresh greens and a little chili.
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.serving: Blanch the vermicelli, arrange the fish and greens in bowls, and ladle over the hot broth. Serve with fresh greens, lime and chili to taste.
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.image_alt: A bowl of Quang Ngai tuna vermicelli soup with tuna, tomato, pineapple and fresh herbs in hot broth.
bun-ca-ngu-um-quang-ngai.time_note: The tuna is seared and then gently braised so it absorbs the seasoning without falling apart.
tips: Pat the tuna very dry before searing so its surface firms up and the pieces hold together while braising.
Braise the fish gently and avoid stirring; check doneness according to the thickness of the slices.
Add boiling water for a lighter broth, then adjust the seasoning.
keywords: Quang Ngai tuna um noodle soup

preparation_steps: Rinse the fish briefly, pat dry and season with a little salt and pepper for 10 minutes. Prepare the tomatoes, pineapple, shallots, lemongrass and turmeric.
Wash and drain the fresh greens; slice the scallions and mince the shallots and garlic.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sear both sides of the tuna until lightly golden; set aside. Sauté the shallots, garlic, lemongrass and turmeric until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and pineapple and stir for 2–3 minutes. Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then season with fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Return the tuna to the pot and braise gently for 12–15 minutes until just cooked. Avoid vigorous stirring so the slices stay intact.
Blanch the vermicelli and divide among bowls. Add the fish and fresh greens, ladle over the broth, top with scallions and serve hot.

keywords: Quang Ngai tuna um noodle soup

rau-don-xao-toi.name: Stir-fried fiddlehead fern with garlic
rau-don-xao-toi.serving_basis: Four servings of fiddlehead ferns quickly stir-fried with garlic to retain their green color and light crunch.
rau-don-xao-toi.description: Fiddlehead fern is a wild mountain vegetable that grows in cool, damp places; its young curled shoots have a distinctive crisp texture. Bep Viet quickly stir-fries it with garlic and plant-based seasonings for a fresh, green side dish.
rau-don-xao-toi.finished_dish: A glossy green plate of just-cooked fiddlehead ferns with lightly crisp shoots, fragrant garlic and little excess liquid.
rau-don-xao-toi.serving: Serve the fern as soon as it is stir-fried, alongside hot rice and other savory or vegetarian dishes.
rau-don-xao-toi.image_alt: A plate of glossy stir-fried fiddlehead fern with curled young shoots and golden garlic slices.
rau-don-xao-toi.time_note: Blanch and stir-fry briefly to preserve the fern's green color and light crunch.
tips: Choose tender young shoots, discard old leaves and rinse several times to remove grit.
Blanch the fern briefly and drain before stir-frying to shorten its time in the pan.
Stir-fry in small batches over high heat and use just enough soy sauce to keep the fern from releasing water.

preparation_steps: Trim the fern, discard tough or bruised parts, rinse thoroughly under running water and drain. Slice the garlic.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Blanch the fern for 20–30 seconds, transfer to cool water and drain very well.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant, without letting it burn.
Add the fern and stir-fry over high heat for 1–2 minutes. Season with soy sauce, salt and a little sugar.
Stir just until tender, sprinkle with pepper and turn off the heat. Serve while hot.

ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.name: Mang Den grilled chicken with bamboo sticky rice
aliases: Lam rice with grilled chicken in the Central Highlands
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.serving_basis: Four servings of golden-skinned grilled chicken with bamboo-cooked sticky rice and sesame-peanut salt.
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.description: Grilled chicken with cơm lam is a familiar highland pairing: fragrant marinated chicken cooked over coals alongside sticky rice steamed in bamboo. Bep Viet has adapted it for home cooking with free-range chicken, aromatic é basil and flexible oven or charcoal methods.
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.finished_dish: Golden, lemongrass-fragrant chicken with juicy meat, paired with chewy bamboo sticky rice and nutty sesame-peanut salt.
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.serving: Cut the chicken into pieces, remove the sticky rice from its bamboo tubes and slice it. Serve with sesame-peanut salt, é basil and fresh greens.
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.image_alt: A platter of Mang Den grilled chicken with sliced chicken, sticky rice cooked in bamboo tubes and sesame-peanut salt.
ga-nuong-com-lam-mang-den.time_note: Roasting time varies with the chicken's size and oven; make sure it is fully cooked before serving.
tips: Soak the sticky rice long enough and drain it so it cooks evenly in the bamboo.
When roasting in an oven, turn the chicken halfway through and check that the thickest part reaches at least 74°C.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes after roasting before carving to retain its juices.
keywords: Mang Den grilled chicken with bamboo sticky rice

preparation_steps: Rinse the sticky rice, soak it for 3 hours and drain. Wash the bamboo tubes and let them drain, leaving one natural end closed.
Mince the lemongrass, garlic and shallots; mix with fish sauce, salt and turmeric. Rub over the chicken and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Place some é basil inside the chicken. Toast the sesame, crush the peanuts and mix with salt to make the dipping salt.
cooking_steps: Fill each bamboo tube about two-thirds full with rice, add enough water to just cover it, and seal the opening with banana leaf.
Roast the bamboo tubes over moderate coals or in a 200°C oven for 45–60 minutes, turning regularly until the rice is tender and the bamboo is lightly charred.
Grill the chicken over coals or roast at 190°C for 60–75 minutes, depending on its size, turning evenly and brushing with a thin layer of honey near the end. Cook it through.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes before carving. Unwrap the bamboo rice, slice it and serve with the sesame-peanut salt and é basil.

banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.name: Tay Ninh vegetarian banh tet
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.serving_basis: One medium vegetarian sticky-rice cake, sliced into about 16 servings.
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.description: This Tay Ninh vegetarian sticky-rice cake wraps mung beans, coconut and sugar in glutinous rice and banana leaves for a gently sweet, nutty flavor. Bep Viet has adapted a family-sized loaf with clear steps for soaking, wrapping and steady simmering.
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.finished_dish: Each slice has fragrant, chewy sticky rice around a mellow mung-bean and coconut filling, neatly wrapped in green banana leaves.
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.serving: Let the cake cool slightly, then slice it with a clean knife for breakfast or a snack. Refrigerate leftovers and reheat thoroughly before eating.
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.image_alt: Tay Ninh vegetarian banh tet wrapped in green banana leaves, sliced to show chewy sticky rice with mung-bean and coconut filling.
banh-tet-chay-tay-ninh.time_note: The rice needs soaking and the cake simmers for several hours; actual cooking time depends on the loaf's size.
tips: Soak the rice and mung beans separately and drain them well before wrapping to prevent a soggy cake.
Wrap the cake firmly and tie it evenly. Add more boiling water if the pot level drops.
Use clean banana leaves and ties; cool promptly and refrigerate any leftovers.

preparation_steps: Rinse the sticky rice, soak for 4 hours and drain. Soak the mung beans for 2 hours, steam until tender and mash.
Cook the mung beans with shredded coconut, some of the sugar, salt and a little coconut milk until cohesive. Cool and shape into a long log.
Mix the rice with the remaining sugar, a little salt and coconut milk. Blanch the banana leaves until pliable, wipe dry and layer them.
cooking_steps: Lay out the banana leaves, spread the rice into a rectangle, place the filling log in the center and cover it completely with rice.
Roll the leaves tightly into a log, fold in the ends and tie evenly so the cake holds its shape while boiling.
Place the cake in boiling water and simmer over medium heat for about 4 hours, topping up with boiling water to keep it submerged.
Remove the cake, briefly rinse the outer leaves with clean water and hang to drain. Cool before slicing.
